title: rfc-8392 CWT Claims Set (derived)
description: DERIVED - not verbatim. RFC 8392 ships no JSON Schema (the string 'JSON Schema' occurs zero times in it). This is the library's machine-checkable rendering of §3.1.1-§3.1.7 and §4 Table 1 over a JSON projection in which a CBOR integer claim key appears as the decimal string of that integer and a CBOR byte string appears as lowercase hex. THE PROJECTION IS OURS: RFC 8392 defines no JSON form and §1 exists precisely to avoid JSON. Use it for fixture validation only, never as a wire format. The CDDL in this directory is the authority on the CBOR.

3.title: aud (§3.1.3). THE ARRAY BRANCH IS §3.1.3's AND IS EXCLUDED BY §4 Table 1 AND §9.1.2 — see design-notes.md defect D-3

7.title: cti (§3.1.7), byte string as lowercase hex

0.title: key 0 is RESERVED by §9.1.2 and may never carry a value

x-library-notes.mandatory-claims: NONE. §3: 'The set of claims that a CWT must contain to be considered valid is context dependent and is outside the scope of this specification.' §3.1: 'None of the claims defined below are intended to be mandatory to use or implement.' The empty object is conformant.
x-library-notes.unknown-claims: additionalProperties is true because §3 requires that 'all claims that are not understood by implementations MUST be ignored'. A schema that rejected them would contradict the source.
x-library-notes.float-claims: exp/nbf/iat are 'integer or floating-point number' per §4 Table 1. Appendix A.7 prints iat as the float64 1443944944.5 (0xfb41d584367c200000); float32 round-trips it to 1443944960.0, so the width is load-bearing. Measured by this extraction.
x-library-notes.no-tags: §5: claim values 'MUST NOT be prefixed with any CBOR tag', and §2 removes tag 1 from NumericDate. A JSON projection cannot express a tag, so this constraint is unenforceable here and lives in the CDDL and in requirements.yaml R-0039 and R-0006.
